topic: Addition and Subtraction of Quadratic Expressions

lessonData.topic: Addition and Subtraction of Quadratic Expressions
lessonData.subject: Mathematics / Algebra
lessonData.tagline: Master the power of powers: combine matching terms and keep the rest intact!
lessonData.overview: A quadratic expression is a polynomial of degree 2 written in the standard form ax² + bx + c where a ≠ 0. When adding or subtracting quadratic expressions, you can only combine like terms—terms sharing identical variables raised to identical powers—by adding or subtracting their numerical coefficients.

diagram.title: Simplifying Quadratic Expressions Workflow
diagram.description: Step-by-step logic for organizing, grouping, and combining terms in quadratic expressions.

nodes.label: Inspect & Expand Signs
nodes.details: Resolve double negatives and distribute any subtraction signs across grouped terms.

nodes.label: Sort Into Term Families
nodes.details: Group terms with identical variable bases and powers. Recognize that xy and yx are identical due to commutativity.

nodes.label: Combine Coefficients
nodes.details: Keep the variable part unchanged and evaluate the coefficients: (a + c)x².

nodes.label: Maintain Unlike Degrees
nodes.details: Terms with different exponents represent completely different geometric dimensions and cannot be added together.

nodes.label: Write in Standard Order
nodes.details: Present the simplified expression descending from highest degree to constant terms.

chalkNotes.title: Adding & Subtracting Quadratic Expressions
chalkNotes.subtitle: Grade 8 Algebra Fundamentals
chalkNotes.coreRuleOrFormula: ax² + bx + c ± (dx² + ex + f) = (a ± d)x² + (b ± e)x + (c ± f)
bulletPoints: Quadratic Form: ax² + bx + c, where a, b, and c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.
Like Terms: Terms with the EXACT same variables and matching exponents (e.g., -8x² and 4x²).
Commutative Property: xy = yx; thus, -3xy and 4yx are like terms and combine to +1xy.
Do NOT Add Exponents: x² + x ≠ x³ and x² + x ≠ 2x²; terms with different powers remain separate.
keyTakeaways: Only coefficients change when adding or subtracting like terms; the variable and power stay unchanged.
Always simplify signs first: subtracting a negative term turns into addition (e.g., -(-9y²) = +9y²).

quiz.question: Simplify the algebraic expression completely: -y² - 3xy - 5y² - (-4yx)
quiz.explanation: First, handle the double negative: -(-4yx) becomes +4yx. Because multiplication is commutative, yx = xy, making -3xy and +4yx like terms. Combine y² terms: -1y² - 5y² = -6y². Combine xy terms: -3xy + 4xy = +1xy. The result is -6y² + xy. Notice that powers are never added when combining like terms (-y² - 5y² is NOT -6y⁴).

suggestedQuestions: Prerequisite Check: How do I simplify 5x - 8x + 2x, and how does this rule apply to x² terms?
Misconception Probe: If x = 3, what is x² + x? Does that equal 3³ or 2(3²)? Why does this prove they can't be combined?
Misconception Probe: Why are -3xy and 4yx considered like terms even though the letters are written in reverse order?

nodes.label: Distribute Operations
nodes.details: Remove brackets, taking special care to distribute the negative sign to all terms if subtracting.

nodes.label: Group Like Terms
nodes.details: Rearrange terms so matching powers are grouped together: quadratic terms, linear terms, and numbers.

key-properties-of-addition-and-subtracti.title: Key Properties of Adding and Subtracting Quadratics
key-properties-of-addition-and-subtracti.description: Essential algebraic properties governing how quadratic expressions are combined and simplified.

nodes.label: Sign Distribution in Subtraction
nodes.details: Subtracting a quadratic requires reversing the signs of every term in the subtracted expression before combining.

nodes.label: Like Terms Alignment
nodes.details: Only coefficients of terms with matching powers can be added or subtracted together.

nodes.label: Commutative & Associative Rules
nodes.sublabel: P + Q = Q + P, but P - Q ≠ Q - P
nodes.details: Addition allows reordering and regrouping of expressions, whereas subtraction is strictly non-commutative.

nodes.label: Degree Closure & Reduction
nodes.details: The result is always a polynomial of degree 2 or less; opposing quadratic terms can cancel out completely.

main.title: Sorting Algebraic Tiles
main.why: It shows that different powers of x represent physically different shapes that cannot combine into a single block.
main.checkQuestion: If I have three x^2 tiles and two x tiles, can I combine them into a single shape? Why or why not?

steps.name: Introducing the Tiles
steps.caption: Algebra uses shapes to represent values: squares for x^2, rectangles for x, and tiny units.

steps.name: Like terms only
steps.caption: You can only combine shapes that are exactly the same type.

contrast:combine-unlike-powers.title: Testing x² + x = x³
contrast:combine-unlike-powers.why: This visual comparison demonstrates that x² (area) and x (length) occupy different dimensions, revealing why they cannot be combined into a single algebraic term.
contrast:combine-unlike-powers.checkQuestion: If you look at the shapes, why can't you combine a square (x^2) and a line (x) into one single term?

steps.name: Draw the shapes
steps.caption: Let's represent x^2 as a square and x as a length.

steps.name: Test the rule
steps.caption: Does adding a length to an area create a 3D volume (x^3)?

steps.name: Check understanding
steps.caption: Notice how area and length cannot merge into a single shape.

contrast:combine-unlike-powers.focus: Terms with the same variable letter but different powers can be added together, e.g., x^2 + x = x^3 or 2x^2.

contrast:order-of-variables-unlike.title: Is xy different from yx?
contrast:order-of-variables-unlike.why: It shows that rearranging the order of factors in multiplication creates an identical area, proving xy and yx are like terms.
contrast:order-of-variables-unlike.checkQuestion: If these rectangles represent the same area, what happens when we combine -3xy and 4yx?

steps.name: Draw two separate rectangles
steps.caption: Let's represent the expressions as areas of rectangles.

steps.name: Compare the expressions
steps.caption: Does the order of variables change the area?

steps.name: Show commutativity
steps.caption: Multiplication is commutative: 3 times 4 is the same as 4 times 3.

steps.name: Check understanding
steps.caption: Since the areas are identical, how can we simplify -3xy + 4yx?

contrast:order-of-variables-unlike.focus: xy and yx are unlike terms because the variables appear in a different order.

apply.title: Simplifying Algebraic Expressions
apply.why: Visualizing terms grouped by type helps the learner see that unlike terms cannot be combined, preventing the common power-addition misconception.
apply.checkQuestion: Before we move the terms, how do we handle the negative sign outside the parenthesis?

steps.name: Introduce categories

3d.title: Why x^2 and x are different
3d.why: Visually demonstrate that areas of squares and rectangles represent different dimensions and thus cannot be combined as like terms.
